artworks.title: Clytemnestra
artworks.description: Collier's queen after the murder that opens Aeschylus' trilogy — bloodied axe, bare feet on the threshold, Agamemnon already dead inside the house the Oresteia must avenge.

artworks.title: Electra at the Tomb of Agamemnon
artworks.description: Leighton's Electra at her father's Mycenaean tomb — the Libation Bearers' vigil before Orestes returns and the axe falls again.

artworks.title: Orestes Pursued by the Furies
artworks.description: Bouguereau's remorse after the matricide — Orestes recoiling as the Erinyes throng, the Oresteia's blood-guilt before Athens' court.

artworks.title: The Ghost of Clytemnestra Awakening the Furies
artworks.description: Downman stages the Eumenides' opening: the murdered queen's shade rises to rouse the sleeping Erinyes against her son Orestes. Clytemnestra appears after death as the engine of the Oresteia's final pursuit — blood calling for blood. Oil on panel, Yale Center for British Art.

films.title: Electra
films.description: Cacoyannis films the Oresteia's core — the son returned, the axe, the mother — in stark Greek light.

music.title: Elektra
music.description: Strauss' one-act nightmare of waiting and the axe — Hofmannsthal's Electra until Orestes strikes.

popCulture.title: Oresteia
popCulture.creator: Aeschylus
popCulture.description: Aeschylus' only surviving trilogy — Agamemnon, the Libation Bearers, the Eumenides — still the West's map of blood-guilt turning into law.

popCulture.title: Electra (Sophocles play)
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: Sophocles' Electra waiting at Mycenae — sister and recognition before the matricide the Oresteia made inevitable.

popCulture.title: Electra (Euripides play)
popCulture.creator: Euripides
popCulture.description: Euripides' rural Electra — the same revenge, colder and more uneasy, the Oresteia's blood without Aeschylus' civic closure.
